data.title: U.S. Bank Completes Live Cross-Border Payment Pilot on Stellar
data.description:
U.S. Bank completed a live cross-border payment pilot with USBDC on Stellar. According to NS3.AI, the payment moved between U.S. Bank entities in North America and Europe.

The announcement did not include a customer access plan, payment amount, or commercial rollout date. It said the pilot was used to test token controls within the bank's own corporate structure.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Venezuela Oil, Renewables Overcapacity, Defense Tech Boom in Focus
data.description:
Venezuela’s oil reserves could affect global energy markets, but rebuilding production would take years, billions of dollars and investor trust, according to Bloomberg.

Europe’s solar success is also creating growing pains for investors, generators and power markets. The report said data centers may be able to turn Scotland’s wasted wind into an AI advantage.

Bloomberg reported that a more dangerous world is pushing the Pentagon and Silicon Valley closer together, fueling a boom in defense and space technologies.

data.title: STOCKS | U.S. Stocks Rebound As Oil Prices Ease And Inflation Data Calms Markets
data.description:
U.S. stocks rebounded on Friday, with the S&P 500 snapping a four-day losing streak after oil prices eased and inflation data came in close to economists’ expectations, according to RTHK. The S&P 500 rose 0.9 percent, the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 509 points, or 1 percent, and the Nasdaq composite added 1 percent.

The S&P 500 climbed 65.28 points to 7,656.98, the Dow Jones Industrial Average added 509.19 to 52,573.29, and the Nasdaq composite rose 251.31 to 26,333.04. Brent crude fell 2.8 percent to settle at US$104.61 after nearing US$110 overnight, easing some pressure on inflation. A Friday report showed U.S. consumers paid prices for gasoline, food and other costs of living that were 3.4 percent higher last month than a year earlier. The data strengthened expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise its main interest rate at its meeting next week.

data.title: Symbiosis Reports Security Incident, Pauses Bitcoin Bridge Routing
data.description:
Cross-chain liquidity protocol Symbiosis said it suffered a security incident after an attacker exploited a Bitcoin bridge vulnerability at about 04:28 UTC on September 11, 2026. According to ChainCatcher, BTC routing has been suspended, while other routes continue to operate normally.

The project said only the Bitcoin bridge was affected and that it has been isolated from other systems. EVM chains, TRON, TON, and other routes, as well as components such as Octopools, were not affected. The team said it has recovered about 15 BTC and placed the funds in a multisig wallet under team control.

Symbiosis said it has offered the attacker a white-hat bounty equal to 20% of the funds, valid until September 13, 2026. After that, the same percentage will be offered to anyone who provides information that helps recover the funds.

Final loss calculations are still underway, and confirmed figures will be released later. The team is contacting affected liquidity providers one by one and is developing a compensation framework. It added that the relay group remains operational and is helping secure the network.

data.title: Mississippi Police Make First Arrest In Death Of Tasia Fortune
data.description:
According to the BBC, police in Jackson, Mississippi, have made their first arrest in the death of Tasia Fortune, a Black woman whose body was found hanging from a tree in August, and said more arrests could follow. Jackson Police Chief RaShall Brackney said the medical examiner had ruled the death a homicide and that a murder charge would be filed against a suspected killer. Police said they had interviewed 15 people in the case.

Fortune's mother, Christy Spivey, said she felt some relief after officers called her on Friday with the update, but said she still hoped police had arrested the right person. She had previously said she struggled to sleep and had tried repeatedly to contact Jackson police without success. Brackney said the department had been in constant contact with Fortune's mother, stepfather and biological father throughout the investigation. More than 50 members of Congress have also sent a letter to the FBI and the Justice Department calling for an independent investigation into suspicious deaths of Black Americans, saying there had been at least 10 reported hangings of Black people in the US this year.

data.title: Andy Burnham Weighs UK Strategy Toward EU as Canada and EU Draft Broad Pact
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham is weighing his strategy toward the EU as Canada and the EU draft a comprehensive agreement covering trade and security. The EU and Canada are working to build a new kind of partnership to counter the United States, which could overshadow the UK-EU summit planned for November. Burnham has begun outlining his European policy, seeking closer ties with the EU while addressing concerns about the impact of the EU's "Made in Europe" plan on British industry.

data.title: Former NYC Deputy Mayor Edward Skyler Reflects on 9/11 Aftermath
data.description:
Edward Skyler said it was extremely difficult to make decisions after 9/11, when 2,700 people were murdered and New York was filled with grief, anxiety and political tension, according to Bloomberg.

He said smoke was still rising from the World Trade Center site when Mayor Bloomberg was sworn in on 01/01/2002, after the economic damage had already been done. Skyler said city leaders had to listen to all sides and make a plan that served New York’s best interests, even if it disappointed some people, and said those decisions have stood the test of time.

data.title: Peskov Says Russia, U.S., and Ukraine May Hold Trilateral Talks Soon
data.description: According to Sina Finance, Russian presidential spokesman Dmitry Peskov said in an interview on September 11 local time that the Kremlin expects Russia, the United States, and Ukraine to hold trilateral talks soon and continue dialogue. data.title: Jim Cramer Says Falling Oil Prices Lifted Stocks, Warns Fed Meeting Could Shift Outlook
data.description:
According to CNBC, Jim Cramer said falling oil prices helped revive stocks on Friday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average up 509 points, or 0.98%, the S&P 500 up 0.86%, and the Nasdaq Composite up 0.96% after four straight down sessions. He said positive after-hours results from Adobe and Oracle helped lift technology shares and renewed interest in enterprise software and data center stocks, naming Dell, Vertiv, Cisco, Marvell, GE Vernova and Hewlett Packard Enterprise as possible beneficiaries.

Cramer said next week’s market direction will depend largely on oil prices and interest rates, with the war in Iran a key variable. He said progress toward peace could push oil lower and ease inflation pressure, while renewed fighting could send oil higher and hurt stocks. He also said the Federal Reserve’s Open Market Committee meets Wednesday and that the consensus expects policymakers to raise rates to combat persistent inflation. Cramer said he will watch how longer-term Treasury yields react and warned that another rate increase would make investing more difficult. He also said Lennar reports after Wednesday’s close, while Brinker International and Intuit hold analyst meetings Thursday.

data.title: JPMorgan Ends Lending Relationship With Situational Awareness After Losses
data.description: According to Sina Finance, citing the Financial Times and people familiar with the matter, JPMorgan Chase has stopped providing loans to Leopold Aschenbrenner's hedge fund, Situational Awareness. JPMorgan had previously financed the fund through its prime brokerage business and was one of its main lenders. After the fund posted losses, JPMorgan told it that the lending relationship would end. Morgan Stanley has been in contact with Situational Awareness since its launch but never established a banking relationship. The Financial Times said JPMorgan, Situational Awareness, and Morgan Stanley all declined to comment.
